result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. The environment is characterized by a one-way street with commercial land use and mature street trees providing some buffer.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra stripes are showing signs of wear, which can reduce visibility for drivers at night or in poor weather.

hazards.name: Lack of curb extensions
hazards.description: The absence of bulb-outs increases the crossing distance and exposure time for pedestrians in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban commercial street with wide, well-maintained sidewalks and a marked crosswalk in the foreground. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the crossing distance is relatively long and sightlines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles along the curb.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb block the line of sight between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the curb line

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two travel lanes and two parking lanes without a median or refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crosswalk to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line markings to a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility to approaching motorists.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk with pedestrian signals and curb ramps at a commercial corner. However, the crossing leads into a dark underpass beneath a large building, which significantly reduces visibility for both drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Dark Underpass Visibility
hazards.description: The building overhang creates a dark tunnel effect that significantly reduces the visibility of pedestrians to drivers entering or exiting the area.
hazards.location_in_image: Center background under the building structure

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing the risk of conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left corner near the fire hydrant

interventions.title: Enhanced Underpass Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity LED lighting under the building overhang to improve visibility and safety for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a well-maintained urban intersection with wide sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and signalized pedestrian controls. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming or dedicated bicycle lanes increase exposure for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge or curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Repurpose a portion of the wide roadway for a protected bike lane to narrow travel lanes and provide a buffer for pedestrians.

interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.
